entities.summary: John II of Werdenberg was a German nobleman and clergyman of the house of Werdenberg, who played a crucial role in shaping the religious landscape of Augsburg during the Late Middle Ages. As Bishop of Augsburg from 1469 until his death in 1486, John II worked to strengthen the city's Catholic institutions and promoted the interests of the local nobility. He was instrumental in the development of the Augsburg Confession, a foundational document of the Protestant Reformation. John II's efforts had a lasting impact on the development of the city, leaving behind a legacy of religious and cultural significance that continues to be felt today. The exact date of his birth is unknown, but his death in 1486 marked the end of an era for the city of Augsburg.\n\n
